download.title: Download Internet Monitor — Windows, Mac, Linux, Pi
download.description: Download Internet Monitor for free and install it in a few minutes, with simple steps for Windows, Mac, Linux and Raspberry Pi.
download.intro: Free, no account needed. Pick your computer below, download one file, and follow the short steps.
download.detected: Looks like you're on {os}. This is the file for you:
download.phone: Internet Monitor runs on a computer. Open this page on your computer to download it. You can then check the dashboard from your phone.

os_sub.mac: Apple chip (M1 and newer) or Intel
os_sub.pi: Runs 24/7, you open it from your phone or PC

download.tray_desc: Runs quietly in the background with a small icon near the clock. Best for catching every outage.
download.window_desc: Opens in its own window, like any other app.
download.mac_arm: Mac with Apple chip (M1, M2, M3, M4…)
download.mac_which: Not sure which Mac you have? Click the Apple menu, then **About This Mac**. If it says **Chip: Apple**, pick Apple chip. If it says **Processor: Intel**, pick Intel.
download.preview_only: Only in the preview for now
download.fallback: We couldn't load the list of files right now. All the files are on the downloads page on GitHub.
download.preview_body: Version {version} ({date}) is a test version with the newest features. It may still have bugs. The app never switches to a preview on its own.
download.install_sub: Takes about two minutes. You only do this once.

windows: Make a new folder, for example **Internet Monitor** in your Documents, and move the file into it. The app keeps its records next to itself.
Double-click the file to start it.
If a blue window says **Windows protected your PC**, click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. This appears because the app is new and not signed, not because something is wrong.
A small icon appears near the clock (click the **^** arrow if you don't see it). Click it and choose **Open dashboard**.
In the dashboard, open **Settings → App** and turn on **Start with Windows**, so it keeps watching after a restart.
mac: Download the file for your Mac above.
Make a new folder, for example **Internet Monitor** in your Documents, and move the file into it.
Open **Terminal** (search for it with Spotlight), type **chmod +x** and a space, drag the file into the Terminal window, and press Enter. This lets the file run.
Right-click the file (or Control-click) and choose **Open**, then **Open** again. You only need to do this the first time.
If your Mac says it **can't be opened because it's from an unidentified developer** and shows no Open button, go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down and click **Open Anyway**.
An icon appears in the menu bar at the top. Click it and choose **Open dashboard**.
linux: Download the file above and move it to a folder of its own.
Right-click the file, choose **Properties → Permissions**, and tick **Allow executing file as program**. Or run **chmod +x** on it in a terminal.
Double-click the file, or run it from a terminal.
Open the dashboard from the tray icon, or from the app window in the window version.
pi: Download the file for your device above.
In a terminal, run **chmod +x** on the file, then start it with **--listen 0.0.0.0** so your phone and PC can reach it.
It prints a link with your private key. Open it from any phone or computer at home.
To start it automatically after a power cut, follow the full guide.

guide.title: Beginner's guide — your first complaint in 5 steps
guide.description: A simple guide to Internet Monitor: install it, leave it running, and send your provider a complaint backed by real measurements.
guide.intro: No technical knowledge needed. Here's how to go from "my internet keeps dropping" to a complaint your provider can't brush off.

steps.title: Install it
steps.body: Download the app for your computer and start it. It takes two minutes, and the download page walks you through it.

steps.title: Leave it running
steps.body: Keep it running in the background, every day. It checks your internet every few seconds. A computer that stays on and is plugged into the router by cable gives the best proof. Times when the computer was off or asleep are marked as "not monitored", never as outages.

steps.title: Fill in your line details
steps.body: Open **Complaints** in the dashboard and enter your country, your provider, your plan speed and your line number. This is saved only on your computer and is used to fill in your complaint.

steps.title: When outages happen, open Complaints
steps.body: The **Your line in the last 7 days** card shows what happened. When your line has dropped, it suggests logging a complaint. Call your provider, then write down the complaint number they give you.

steps.title: Send the proof
steps.body: Open your complaint and press **Copy text** to get a ready-made message with your outages, downtime and speed. Press **Download evidence (ZIP)** to get the proof file, and send both to your provider. If they don't answer in time, the page shows you how to go to the regulator.

tips: The monthly report (History → Monthly report → Print or save as PDF) covers the whole month in one page.
Turn on scheduled speed tests in Settings to show your speed over time, not just once.
Alerts can reach your phone through Telegram, Discord or ntfy when the internet drops.
guide.pi_title: Run it 24/7 on a Raspberry Pi
guide.pi_intro: The strongest proof comes from a device that never sleeps. A laptop that goes to sleep leaves gaps. A small Raspberry Pi plugged into your router by cable watches all day and night, and you open the dashboard from your phone.
pi_steps: Download the Raspberry Pi file: **arm64** for a Pi 4 or 5, **armv7** for a Pi 2 or 3.
Make it runnable and start it with **--listen 0.0.0.0**, so other devices at home can reach it.
It prints a link (and a QR code) with your private key. Scan it with your phone's camera and the dashboard opens. Keep this link private.
Set it to start on its own after a power cut, using the few lines in the full guide. It also runs with Docker.
